mainEntity.name: What is the Early Years Programme (EYP) at VGWS?

mainEntity.name: What skills does EYP build before a child moves into PYP proper?

mainEntity.name: How is the IB different from CBSE at a structural level?

acceptedAnswer.text: The IB Organisation (IBO) is a non-profit that provides a flexible framework across four programmes — PYP, MYP, DP and CP — rather than a single fixed national curriculum. CBSE is a national board delivering one prescribed syllabus per subject with centrally set board examinations, while IB assessment varies by stage: open-ended in PYP, e-examinations in MYP, and centrally moderated Diploma exams (assessed from Cardiff and Geneva) in Grade 12.

mainEntity.name: Which is more exam-focused — IB or CBSE?

acceptedAnswer.text: CBSE is structured around scoring well in centralised board examinations at Class / Grade 10 and 12 with rote learning & memorization pattern. But where as IB, particularly through PYP and MYP, is built around inquiry and conceptual understanding throughout the years, with the DP's final exams complemented by continuous internal assessment, TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS — so the IB spreads assessment across skills, research and reflection rather than concentrating it in a single high-stakes exam period.

acceptedAnswer.text: Following what the school calls 'Gurukulian tradition,' the ceremony opens with the World Peace Prayer and the Lighting of the Lamp by dignitaries, followed by cultural performances such as a prayer dance (e.g., 'Ganesh Vandana') and shloka recitations by DP-1 students, before the formal Badge and Sash Ceremony and oath-taking.

mainEntity.name: What is the Badge and Sash Ceremony?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the ceremonial core of the event — newly elected student leaders are formally presented with badges and sashes that symbolise their transition into leadership roles, each badge marking a specific office (Head Boy/Girl, House Captain, Prefect, and so on).

mainEntity.name: What oath do the newly inducted student leaders take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The elected Prefect Body takes an oath promising to carry out their duties with integrity and to uphold the school's traditions, administered by a senior staff member — for instance, the AY2023-24 oath was led by Ms. Sneha Bhatt.

mainEntity.name: What is VGWS's house system for the Investiture Ceremony, and how is it different from the boarding houses?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Student Council and Investiture purposes, VGWS uses four elemental houses — Agni, Jal, Prithvi and Vayu — spanning the PYP, MYP and DP sections. This is a separate structure from VGWS's four residential boarding houses (Bharadwaj, Jamadagni, Kashyapa and Vashistha, named after Vedic sages), which organise day-to-day boarding life rather than student council elections.

mainEntity.name: What are the four Investiture houses, and what do their mottos represent?

acceptedAnswer.text: Agni House (symbol: Phoenix) represents resilience and rebirth, with the motto 'Arise, Awake & Stop Not Till the Goal is Reached.' Prithvi House stands for peace and prosperity ('Shanti Samridhi'). Jal House represents compassion and healing, with the motto 'Flowing towards excellence.' Vayu House symbolises inner strength and intuition, with the motto 'Nil Desperandum' ('Never give up').

mainEntity.name: What leadership positions are conferred at the ceremony?

acceptedAnswer.text: Positions include Head Boy and Head Girl, School Sports Captains (male and female), School Cultural Captains (male and female), House Captains, House Sports Captains, House Cultural Captains, and Deputy House Captains — elected separately across the PYP, MYP and DP sections of each house — alongside Boarding Prefects representing the residential community.

mainEntity.name: Can you give an example of a past VGWS Prefect Council?

acceptedAnswer.text: For AY2024-25, the Prefect Council included Head Boy Rohan George and Head Girl Shreya Katariya, School Sports Captains Omraj Karle (male) and Kanishka M. Maniya (female), and School Cultural Captains Eshaan Khandelwal (male) and Kristina Sabarna (female), alongside House Captains, Sports Captains and Cultural Captains elected across Agni, Jal, Prithvi and Vayu houses and every section from PYP through DP.

mainEntity.name: How are student council leaders selected at VGWS?

acceptedAnswer.text: The school describes the process as an election — the Investiture Ceremony 'celebrat[es] the election of new student leaders and prefects,' with newly elected office bearers formally announced and inducted at the ceremony itself.

mainEntity.name: Does the Investiture Ceremony include both day scholars and boarding students?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — leadership positions are conferred across every section (PYP, MYP, DP) and explicitly include Boarding Prefects alongside day-section student leaders, reflecting VGWS's combined day-cum-boarding structure and its commitment to leadership opportunity regardless of boarding status.

mainEntity.name: Who typically addresses the students at the ceremony?

acceptedAnswer.text: Past ceremonies have featured keynote addresses from senior academic leadership — for example, the AY2026-27 ceremony featured an address from the HOS, Mr.Vidhukesh Vimal, motivating students to aim high, with a Vote of Thanks proposed by a senior DP coordinator. Head Boys and Head Girls also address the school directly as part of the ceremony.

mainEntity.name: What did VGWS's Head Boy and Head Girl speak about in a recent Investiture Ceremony?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the AY2026-27 ceremony, Head Boy Siddant Nande spoke about the power of teamwork and unity, while Head Girl Chandni Bhatia focused on resilience and kindness, urging fellow students to lead through compassion and courage rather than treating leadership as a position of authority alone.

mainEntity.name: Was there anything notable about the VGWS Investiture Ceremony for AY2026-27?

acceptedAnswer.text: In sharing the 2026-27 ceremony publicly, VGWS's Chief Administrative Officer reflected that a school's character is 'sometimes... defined by a single act of compassion,' noting that one newly appointed Head Boy could not be present at the ceremony as he was hospitalised — a moment the school highlighted as reflecting its values of care and community alongside the formal induction of the new student council.

mainEntity.name: How does the Investiture Ceremony connect to VGWS's broader leadership-development philosophy?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the formal starting point of a leadership journey that continues through the year via the boarding house system, the Student Well-Being Council, student-led clubs, MUN and CAS — the ceremony itself frames leadership explicitly as 'an opportunity to make a meaningful impact,' not merely a title, consistent with VGWS's wider values-based approach to student leadership.

mainEntity.name: Are Indian cultural and spiritual elements part of the Investiture Ceremony?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — the ceremony's opening World Peace Prayer, Lamp Lighting, and shloka/prayer-dance performances by DP-1 students reflect VGWS's Guru-Shishya-rooted approach to school life, weaving Indian tradition directly into what is otherwise a Western-style school leadership investiture format.
